decision_description: Conflict between the constitutional-compliance-check artifact's §13.4 violation finding (resolution_status: 'unresolved', severity: 'critical') and the Tier 4 phase output evidence present in canonical inputs. The compliance check (docs/tier4_orchestration_state/validation_reports/constitutional-compliance-check_msca-pf-.json) flagged CLAUDE.md §13.4 as a critical violation because docs/tier4_orchestration_state/phase_outputs/phase7_budget_gate/budget_gate_assessment.json was outside the TAPM input boundary of the constitutional-compliance-check skill invocation and its gate_pass_declaration could not be confirmed from within that execution context. Canonical Tier 4 inputs to this decision-log-update invocation confirm: (1) budget_gate_assessment.json carries gate_pass_declaration: 'pass' and instrument_type_note confirming MSCA-PF unit-cost path per CLAUDE.md §8.4 C1 amendment; (2) gate_result.json carries status: 'pass', gate_id: 'gate_09_budget_consistency', evaluated_at: '2026-07-16T22:36:25.729770+00:00' — six days prior to the review packet production timestamp of 2026-07-22T00:00:00Z. Tiers in conflict: Tier 4 phase_outputs/phase7_budget_gate/ (documents gate passage) vs. the compliance check validation report (could not confirm gate passage within TAPM boundary). Per CLAUDE.md §9.3, Tier 4 documented state governs over agent memory and runtime tool-boundary limitations. Resolution: the §13.4 violation is resolved in favour of Tier 4 documented state; gate_09 passed before Phase 8 commenced. Three remaining violations identified in the compliance check (§13.2: review_packet.json asserts Tier 2A/2B evaluation sub-criteria without traceability_footer; §13.3: review_packet.json names Tier 3 project facts without traceability_footer; §13.10: review_packet.json entirely absent a traceability_footer) remain unresolved and are not affected by this resolution — they concern genuine structural gaps in the review_packet.json artifact requiring human operator action or artifact revision.
alternatives_considered: Accept the compliance check §13.4 finding as unresolved pending explicit human operator confirmation — rejected because the canonical budget_gate_assessment.json and gate_result.json are provided as inputs to this skill invocation and unambiguously confirm gate_09_budget_consistency passed on 2026-07-16T22:36:25.729770+00:00, prior to Phase 8; CLAUDE.md §9.3 requires Tier 4 documented state to govern over a prior skill invocation's TAPM boundary limitation, and preferring fabricated non-resolution over documented evidence would itself be a constitutional violation

Treat the TAPM boundary limitation of the compliance-check skill as an independent constitutional violation warranting a separate entry — rejected because the TAPM boundary is a runtime execution constraint governed by §17 migration architecture, not a §13 prohibited action; the question of budget gate passage is fully resolved by Tier 4 artifacts, and the compliance check correctly applied fail-closed semantics (CLAUDE.md §15) given its input constraints
tier_authority_applied: CLAUDE.md §9.3 — documented Tier 4 state governs over agent memory and runtime tool-boundary limitations; Tier 4 docs/tier4_orchestration_state/phase_outputs/phase7_budget_gate/budget_gate_assessment.json (gate_pass_declaration: 'pass', instrument_type_note confirming MSCA-PF unit-cost path per §8.4 C1) and Tier 4 docs/tier4_orchestration_state/phase_outputs/phase7_budget_gate/gate_result.json (status: 'pass', gate_id: 'gate_09_budget_consistency', evaluated_at: '2026-07-16T22:36:25.729770+00:00') are the governing authority over the TAPM-bounded compliance check finding; CLAUDE.md §8.4 (instrument-conditional budget gate, unit-cost path) confirms the correct gate mechanism for MSCA-PF
rationale: The constitutional-compliance-check skill invocation correctly applied fail-closed semantics (CLAUDE.md §15: prefer explicit gate failure over fabricated completion) when it could not confirm the budget gate assessment from within its TAPM input boundary, recording §13.4 as a critical unresolved violation. This is the correct behaviour for that skill in that execution context. The decision-log-update skill invocation for this entry receives budget_gate_assessment.json and gate_result.json as canonical inputs. Both confirm gate_09_budget_consistency evaluated to 'pass' on 2026-07-16T22:36:25.729770+00:00, six days before the review packet was produced on 2026-07-22T00:00:00Z. The budget regime is confirmed as unit_cost per CLAUDE.md §8.1 C1 constitutional amendment; all four unit-cost line items carry status 'Confirmed'; unresolved_components is empty; blocking_inconsistencies is empty. Per CLAUDE.md §9.3, when a conflict exists between a prior execution artifact (the compliance check finding) and documented Tier 4 state (budget_gate_assessment.json, gate_result.json), documented Tier 4 state governs. The §13.4 apparent violation is an artifact of TAPM input boundary scoping during the compliance check skill run, not evidence of actual constitutional non-compliance in the workflow. This resolution is durable: it is written to the Tier 4 decision log per §9.4 and may not be held only in agent memory. The three remaining unresolved violations (§13.2, §13.3, §13.10) address the review_packet.json's structural absence of a traceability_footer and require separate corrective action; they are noted here for completeness but are not resolved by this entry.
